title: Why does the line through the centres cut XY in half at a right angle?
description: Two points A and B are the same distance from X and from Y. Two pairs of congruent triangles show that the line A B meets X Y at its middle point and at a right angle. Keeko's doubt, that the triangles are congruent because they look the same, is broken by naming a rule.
teaching_notes: One idea: first side side side gives equal angles at A, then side angle side gives equal sides and equal angles at O. Watch for students who call triangles congruent because they look alike.

source: Points A and B satisfy AX = AY = BX = BY, and AB meets XY at
video_script.why: The child has seen that joining the two meeting points seems to cut X Y in half at a right angle, but has not yet proved it.
video_script.substitution: Two pairs of congruent triangles carry the proof: first the two big triangles on A B, then the two small triangles at O.
video_script.anchor: Points A and B with AX = AY = BX = BY, and the line AB meeting the segment XY at O.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko calls the two small triangles at O congruent because they look the same, without naming a rule or showing three equal parts.
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh B is the perpendicular bisector of X Y

final_answer.value: ΔABX ≅ ΔABY by SSS, then ΔAOX ≅ ΔAOY by SAS; so OX = OY and ∠AOX = ∠AOY = 90°: AB is the perpendicular bisector of XY
final_answer.spoken: eigh B is the perpendicular bisector of X Y, O is its midpoint, and each angle at O is ninety degrees

never_show: the word bisector before the answer line
maths_rules: Given AX = AY and BX = BY; AB is common to triangles ABX and ABY, so triangle ABX is congruent to triangle ABY by SSS.
Corresponding parts are equal, so angle XAB = angle YAB, that is angle XAO = angle YAO, because O lies on AB.
In triangles AOX and AOY: AX = AY, angle XAO = angle YAO, AO is common, so they are congruent by SAS.
So OX = OY (O is the midpoint of XY) and angle AOX = angle AOY.
Angle AOX + angle AOY = 180 degrees (straight angle), and the two are equal, so each is 180 / 2 = 90 degrees.
video_script.design: One idea: two congruences in a chain. Triangles ABX and ABY by SSS give the equal angles at A. Triangles AOX and AOY by SAS give the midpoint and the right angles. Keeko's doubt is that looking alike is enough.
